name: inprocess-obi-wb-uart-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches one real classic Wishbone register target in one process: the ZipCPU UART as a word-addressed registered-ack beat_to_wishbone target. The case line states the cyc/stb/ack/we/adr/dat_w/dat_r/sel handshake the slave's own pins carried, and the summary states the target's protocol and bridge.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one Wishbone classic target at 0x40001000 behind the real beat_to_wishbone adapter (the target profile's own protocol is wishbone/classic and its capabilities declare has_address_port true, sel_implemented true and wishbone_flavour registered-ack).

The generic wishbone_register_observe kernel is the one used: it exposes the slave's cyc/stb/we/adr/dat_w/sel/ack/dat_r (and stall) as passive trace ports, so every case states the handshake it sampled. The specialised wishbone_timer kind is refused by name because its trace has no ack/dat_r and no address port; an addressless zipcpu_timer request is refused before any RTL with unsupported-target-trace:wishbone:addressless:...

Window: the UART's 16 bytes (SETUP(0, rw, write_resets_uart_state), FIFO_STATUS(4, ro), RXREG(8, rw, read pops the RX FIFO), TXREG(12, rw, write pushes the TX FIFO)). It does not overlap the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and clears the 4 GiB bound.
rx=1 and cts_n=0 are the same pin constants the single-target AXI4-Lite scenario declares for the same UART RTL; they are the two non-bus inputs the wishbone register template requires an owner for.

No behavior file is declared: this target declares no F5 facts, so F5 is refused by name (unsupported-f5:target-protocol-not-run:wishbone:wbuart would apply if it did declare them), and the summary states target0_f5 no. No DMA is declared, so F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:Wishbone.
The profile declares 50 MHz, the same as the CPU, so one host tick drives both models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.
